clue.text: Spray cap with inner spring

indicators.note: having an inner part means something sits inside the outer word

blocks.note: to cap a story is to better it
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Someone sprays a cap that has a coiled spring inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' is the verb, to top or outdo, and 'spring' is a source of water, not a coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to splash or sprinkle all over, a verb synonym of spray.

clue.text: E.g. man's attempt to keep record up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the record's letters are read from bottom to top
the attempt keeps something held inside it

blocks.note: a bid is an attempt
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A man tries hard to keep a record-breaking run going.
explanation.definitionFit: Humans walk on two legs, so a man is one example of a two-footed animal.

clue.text: Maintain unfinished saw I'd installed for IT company

indicators.note: something unfinished stops short, so its final letter is lost
what is installed is put inside something else

blocks.note: to service a car is to maintain it
a saw is a proverb; minus its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm's technician keeps a power saw running for a computer company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is the old word for a saying, not the tool: PROVERB loses its B, and ID sits inside, PROV-ID-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A service provider is a business supplying internet or other IT services, such as broadband access.

clue.text: Alcohol confined to labs, in theory

indicators.note: the letters are held within the following words rather than standing alone

blocks.note: the letters run across these three words

explanation.surface: In theory, drinking is something kept within laboratory walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Absinthe is a strong green aniseed spirit, a specific example of alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Primate in two remote marshes primarily an invasive species?

indicators.note: one thing placed in another word means sitting inside it
primarily points to the leading letter of each of the words just before it

blocks.note: taken as written; it holds the primate
an ape is a primate
first letters of remote and marshes

explanation.surface: A monkey turning up in two distant wetlands might count as an invasive species.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a parasite invades its host's body, so the whole clue hints at the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a parasite that invades the gut of its host, so it is jokingly an invasive species.

clue.text: Rouen's top priest there holding large riotous mass

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
the priest holds something inside him

blocks.note: first letter of Rouen
an abbé is a French priest, as found in Rouen
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: The senior cleric of Rouen holds a large, rowdy Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' refers back to Rouen, so the priest is French: ABBE, which takes L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabble is a disorderly crowd, which matches a riotous mass of people.

clue.text: Take to the saddle on escaping from hurricane

indicators.note: what escapes from the storm word leaves it, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters leave
a cyclone is a hurricane

explanation.surface: Someone gets on a bike to escape a hurricane.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ON out of CYCLONE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cycle is to ride a bicycle, i.e. sit on its seat and pedal.

clue.text: High-flying American working party in credit

indicators.note: these go in the credit word, sitting between its letters

blocks.note: CR is the abbreviation for credit; it wraps the rest
a machine that is on is working
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A successful American working for a political party is in the black.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flying' suggests a successful executive, but it means literally flying high.
explanation.definitionFit: The condor is a huge vulture of the Americas that soars at great heights.

clue.text: Another offer from tipsy soprano couple disheartened tenor

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so these letters are jumbled
losing the heart leaves only the outer letters of the word

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
outer letters of tenor

explanation.surface: A drunken soprano and a downcast tenor make an alternative bid.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterproposal is a second offer made in reply to the first one in a negotiation.

clue.text: Third of total fish within boundary caught

indicators.note: the third letter of the next word is the one kept
these letters go within the boundary word

blocks.note: an end is a boundary; it wraps the rest
third letter of total
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A third of the total catch is landed inside the cricket boundary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something entangled is snared or trapped, as a fish is caught in a net.

clue.text: Benefits at university rallies

blocks.note: perks are job benefits
to be up is to be at university

explanation.surface: Staff benefits at a university, or student rallies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At university' gives UP in the British sense of being up at Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To perk up is to recover spirits or energy, the intransitive verb sense of rally.

clue.text: Outlaw still short of one really good meal

indicators.note: short of a thing means lacking it, so that letter goes

blocks.note: to ban is to outlaw
still means quiet
I is the Roman numeral one; it is removed

explanation.surface: An outlaw still lacks a single decent meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun, a bandit, but it is the verb ban.
explanation.definitionFit: A banquet is a lavish formal feast, an elaborate and excellent meal.

clue.text: Condescend, broadcasting Hans Andersen perhaps

indicators.note: broadcasting puts something on air, so the word is heard, not seen

blocks.note: Hans Christian Andersen was Danish

explanation.surface: Someone stoops to reading out a fairy tale on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To deign is to do something one considers beneath one's dignity, the verb sense of condescend.

clue.text: Desert hero ultimately stopping return of non-British rule?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
stopping a gap means plugging it, so this sits inside
a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: not UK, i.e. not British
a law is a rule
last letter of hero

explanation.surface: A desert hero ends the return of foreign rule, like a colonial liberator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like sand in this surface but is the verb to abandon; UK is the standard shorthand for British.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk out on someone is to abandon them, the verb sense of desert.

clue.text: Complex chapter framing current statistician's plan

indicators.note: complex means intricately mixed, so these letters are rearranged
a frame goes around a picture, so these letters surround the next item

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An intricate book chapter frames the latest figures in a statistician's plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A pie chart is a circular diagram of proportions, a layout statisticians use to display data.

clue.text: Treated members with sole, changing dud recipe

indicators.note: changing the words alters the order of their letters

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Diners got fish served as a sole dish when a bad recipe had to be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sole' looks like the fish, but the members are feet, which have soles.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedicured feet have received cosmetic care, and feet are limbs with a sole underneath.

clue.text: Examination of country's past dropped

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: pastoral means of the countryside
taken as written; these letters go

explanation.surface: A test of a nation's history has been abandoned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is not a nation but the countryside: PASTORAL, which loses PAST.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken test, a noun sense of examination in schools and universities.

clue.text: Insinuates that man's a saint, supporting wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath, so the wife comes on top

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
his means the man's
per means a, as in once per day
S is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a man is a saint, backing up his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' stands for per, as in once a day meaning once per day.
explanation.definitionFit: To whisper rumours is to hint at things quietly and indirectly, as one insinuates.

clue.text: Mesmeric character close to tears leaving ground

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
ground means crushed and broken, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: last letter of tears
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hypnotic figure, almost in tears, leaves the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
explanation.definitionFit: Svengali, the hypnotist of Trilby, gave his name to anyone who controls others by mesmerism.

clue.text: Blade for piercing tip of darning needle

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of darning
to needle someone is to irk them

explanation.surface: A sharp point at the end of a darning needle is meant for piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needle' is the verb, to annoy, not the sewing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a short stabbing dagger, a weapon with a blade designed to pierce.

clue.text: Fragmented particle the lecturer's introduced

indicators.note: something introduced is brought inside, placed among other letters

blocks.note: a shred is a tiny particle; it wraps the rest
a lecturer speaking of himself would say I've

explanation.surface: A physics lecturer describes a particle that broke apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The lecturer's' means what the lecturer would say for 'I have', the contraction I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is to break into splinters, so shivered means smashed into fragments.

clue.text: Sullen and cross in past

indicators.note: the cross is placed in the word for past

blocks.note: going past is going by; it wraps the rest
a rood is a crucifix

explanation.surface: Someone who was grumpy and angry in days gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' suggests angry beside sullen, but it is the church cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Broody can mean moody and gloomy, sitting in silent resentment, as a sullen person does.

clue.text: Adversary bound to disregard English rank

indicators.note: to disregard a letter is to ignore it, so it is left out

blocks.note: a foe is an adversary
bound means tied
E is the abbreviation for English; it goes

explanation.surface: An enemy is bound to ignore English rank and status.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' looks like a noun meaning status, but it is the adjective for foul-smelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Foetid means stinking, which is the adjective sense of rank, as in rank odour.

clue.text: Captain Ahab initially runs in from vessel, gaping

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words before it
one thing runs in to the next word, sitting inside it

blocks.note: first letters of Captain and Ahab
venous means relating to a blood vessel; it wraps the next letter
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Captain Ahab rushes in from his ship, staring open-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests Ahab's whaler, but it is a blood vessel, giving the adjective VENOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cavernous means vast and hollow like a cave, so it describes a gaping space.

clue.text: Land beginning to erode in northern China

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter
the letter sits in the following words, inside them

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
first letter of erode
in rhyming slang, china plate means mate, a pal

explanation.surface: Land begins to wear away in the north of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like Nepal's neighbour, but it is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepal is a Himalayan country, and land is used here for a nation.

clue.text: Concrete mounts securing small, light device

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means climbing, so the word is read upwards
securing something means holding it inside

blocks.note: concrete means real, actual
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Concrete mountings hold a small lamp in place.
explanation.walkthrough: REAL read upwards is LAER, which takes S inside: LA-S-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser is an apparatus emitting an intense beam of light, so it is a light device.

clue.text: Old British soldier died, breaking cover again

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: to recoat is to cover again; it wraps the rest
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: An old soldier died, having broken cover once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcoat was the nickname for a British infantryman of earlier centuries, from the scarlet uniform.

clue.text: Sleep as criminal goes by

indicators.note: something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Time passes while a criminal sleeps.
explanation.definitionFit: Time elapses when it passes, so the verb means the same as going by.

clue.text: Salacious verse an essential in education for the first time

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter swaps in where the first instance of another stood

blocks.note: a ditty is a short song or verse
R is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic
T is the abbreviation for time; the first one is replaced

explanation.surface: Racy verse appears in a sex-education lesson for the first time.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces the first T in DITTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty means smutty or lewd, a direct synonym of salacious.

clue.text: Disparage director on board, an Irish manufacturer?

blocks.note: to dis someone is to disparage them
the tiller directs a boat's course

explanation.surface: A board member runs down a director at an Irish manufacturing firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a company board, but the director is a tiller on a boat. The question mark marks a definition by example: an Irish whiskey maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is famed for whiskey, so a distiller is one likely kind of Irish producer.
